What is the smaller angle between the hands of a clock at 3:00?
questions.explanation: At 3:00 the minute hand is at 12 and the hour hand is at 3, a separation of 3×30° = 90°.

questions.stem: What angle do the hour and minute hands form at 6:00?
questions.explanation: The hands point in opposite directions at 6:00, so the angle is 180°.

questions.stem: Through how many degrees does the minute hand move in 20 minutes?
questions.explanation: The minute hand moves 360° in 60 minutes, or 6° per minute. In 20 minutes it moves 20×6° = 120°.

questions.stem: Through how many degrees does the hour hand move in 2 hours 30 minutes?
questions.explanation: The hour hand moves 30° per hour. In 2.5 hours it moves 2.5×30° = 75°.

questions.stem: Find the smaller angle between the hands at 2:30.
questions.explanation: At 2:30, the hour hand is at 2×30°+30×0.5° = 75°, while the minute hand is at 180°. The difference is 105°.

questions.stem: At which of the following times are the two hands exactly together?
questions.explanation: At 12:00 both hands point to 12. At the other listed times they are separated.

questions.stem: A wall clock shows 8:20. What time would its mirror image show?
questions.explanation: For an analogue clock, mirror time = 11:60 − actual time. Thus 11:60−8:20 = 3:40.

questions.stem: A clock loses 5 minutes every day. How much time will it lose in 6 days?
questions.explanation: Total loss = 6×5 = 30 minutes.

questions.stem: A clock gains 2 minutes every hour. How much will it gain in 10 hours?
questions.explanation: Gain = 10×2 = 20 minutes.

questions.stem: How many complete revolutions does the second hand make in 5 minutes?
questions.explanation: The second hand makes one revolution per minute, so it makes 5 revolutions in 5 minutes.

questions.stem: What is the smaller angle between the clock hands at 4:20?
questions.explanation: Hour-hand angle = 4×30+20×0.5 = 130°. Minute-hand angle = 20×6 = 120°. Difference = 10°.

questions.stem: At what time between 2:00 and 3:00 do the hands coincide?
questions.explanation: At m minutes after 2, coincidence requires 60+0.5m = 6m. Hence 5.5m=60 and m=120/11=10 10/11 minutes.

questions.stem: What is the first time after 5:00 when the hands are at right angles?
questions.explanation: At m minutes after 5, |150−5.5m|=90. The earlier solution is 150−5.5m=90, giving m=120/11=10 10/11.

questions.stem: At what time between 7:00 and 8:00 are the hands first in a straight line but pointing in opposite directions?
questions.explanation: At m minutes after 7, |210−5.5m|=180. The feasible early solution is 210−5.5m=180, so m=60/11=5 5/11 minutes.

questions.stem: The mirror image of a clock reads 2:35. What is the actual time?
A slow clock loses 3 minutes every 2 actual hours. It is set correctly at noon. What will it show 20 actual hours later?
questions.explanation: In 20 hours there are ten 2-hour blocks, so the clock loses 30 minutes. It shows an elapsed time of 19 hours 30 minutes, i.e. 7:30 a.m. the next day.

questions.stem: A clock gains 5 minutes every 12 hours. It is correct at 8:00 a.m. on Monday. What will it show at the actual time 8:00 a.m. on Friday?
questions.explanation: The elapsed time is 96 hours, or eight 12-hour blocks. The clock gains 8×5 = 40 minutes, so it shows 8:40 a.m.

questions.stem: How far does the hour hand move while the minute hand completes 40 minutes?
questions.explanation: The hour hand moves 0.5° per minute. In 40 minutes it moves 20°.

questions.stem: How many times do the hour and minute hands coincide in 12 hours?
questions.explanation: The minute hand gains one full revolution on the hour hand 11 times in 12 hours.

questions.stem: How many times are the hour and minute hands at right angles in 12 hours?
questions.explanation: There are two right-angle positions in each relative revolution, and 11 relative revolutions occur in 12 hours. Hence 22 right angles.

questions.stem: How many times are the hands in a straight line and pointing in opposite directions during 12 hours?
questions.explanation: The hands are opposite once in each of the 11 relative revolutions completed in 12 hours.

questions.stem: When do the hands first coincide after 12 noon?
questions.explanation: The minute hand gains on the hour hand at 5.5° per minute. To gain 360°, it needs 360/5.5 = 720/11 = 65 5/11 minutes, giving 1:05 5/11.

questions.stem: A clock takes 24 seconds to strike 7. How many seconds will it take to strike 10 at the same uniform rate?
questions.explanation: Seven strikes contain 6 intervals, so each interval lasts 24/6 = 4 seconds. Ten strikes contain 9 intervals, requiring 9×4 = 36 seconds.

questions.stem: A digital clock uses the 24-hour format. How many times from 00:00 through 23:59 does it display four identical digits?
questions.explanation: The valid displays are 00:00, 11:11 and 22:22. Thus there are 3 such times.

questions.stem: At which two times between 8:00 and 9:00 is the smaller angle between the hands 60°?
A clock is set correctly at noon. At the actual time 6:00 p.m. it shows 6:15 p.m. At the same constant rate, how many minutes will it gain in 24 actual hours?
questions.explanation: It gains 15 minutes in 6 hours. In 24 hours it gains 15×4 = 60 minutes.

questions.stem: Clock A gains 4 minutes per day while Clock B loses 6 minutes per day. Both are set correctly together. After how many days will their readings differ by exactly one hour?
questions.explanation: Their relative divergence is 4+6 = 10 minutes per day. To differ by 60 minutes they need 60/10 = 6 days.

questions.stem: Between 4:00 and 5:00, when are the hour and minute hands equally far from the 12 o’clock position but on opposite sides of it?
questions.explanation: At m minutes after 4, the clockwise angle of the hour hand from 12 is 120+0.5m. The counter-clockwise angle of the minute hand from 12 is 360−6m. Equating them gives 120+0.5m=360−6m, so m=480/13=36 12/13 minutes.

questions.stem: A clock loses 2 minutes every 3 hours. It is correct at 6:00 a.m. What time will its mirror image show at the actual time 6:00 p.m. the same day?
questions.explanation: Over 12 actual hours it loses 8 minutes, so it shows 5:52 p.m. The mirror image of 5:52 is 6:08.

questions.stem: How many times in 24 hours is the smaller angle between the hour and minute hands exactly 60°?
questions.explanation: For an angle strictly between 0° and 180°, there are 22 occurrences in 12 hours. Therefore there are 44 in 24 hours.

questions.stem: What is the smaller angle between the hands at 7:38?
questions.explanation: Hour hand = 7×30+38×0.5 = 229°. Minute hand = 38×6 = 228°. The smaller angle is 1°.

questions.stem: Between 3:00 and 4:00, when are the hands separated by 20 minute divisions on the dial?
questions.explanation: Twenty minute divisions correspond to 120°. Solve |90−5.5m|=120. The feasible solution is m=420/11=38 2/11 minutes.

questions.stem: A tower clock takes 42 seconds to strike 8. How long does it take to strike 12?
questions.explanation: Eight strikes have 7 intervals, each lasting 42/7 = 6 seconds. Twelve strikes have 11 intervals, so the duration is 66 seconds.

questions.stem: After 4:00, when do the two hands next divide the clock face into arcs in the ratio 1:2?
questions.explanation: An arc ratio 1:2 corresponds to a smaller angle of 120°. At 4:m, |120−5.5m|=120. Besides m=0, the next solution is m=240/5.5=480/11=43 7/11.

questions.stem:
What is the exact time between 6:00 and 7:00?

**Statement I:** The hands are at right angles.

**Statement II:** The minute hand is before the 30-minute mark.
questions.explanation: Statement I gives two possible right-angle times in the hour. Statement II selects the earlier one, so together the statements determine the time; neither alone does.

options.label: Statement I alone is sufficient, but Statement II alone is not sufficient.
Statement II alone is sufficient, but Statement I alone is not sufficient.
Both statements together are sufficient, but neither statement alone is sufficient.
Even both statements together are not sufficient.

questions.stem: A clock that loses 4 minutes per day is set correctly. After how many days will its 12-hour dial first show the correct reading again?
questions.explanation: The dial reading agrees again after the clock has lost 12 hours = 720 minutes. At 4 minutes per day, this takes 720/4 = 180 days.

questions.stem: From 12:00 inclusive up to but not including 1:00, how many times do the second and minute hands coincide?
questions.explanation: Their relative speed is 6−0.1 = 5.9° per second, so coincidences are 3600/59 seconds apart. In [0,3600) the multiples k·3600/59 for k=0,…,58 give 59 coincidences.

questions.stem: A defective clock’s minute hand completes one revolution in 72 minutes, while its hour hand works normally. Starting together at noon, after how many actual minutes do the hands next coincide?
questions.explanation: The minute hand moves at 5° per minute and the hour hand at 0.5° per minute. Relative speed = 4.5° per minute, so gaining 360° takes 80 minutes.

questions.stem: A mirror image of a clock shows 10:18. The clock itself is 7 minutes fast. What is the correct time?
questions.explanation: The clock reading is 11:60−10:18 = 1:42. Since it is 7 minutes fast, the correct time is 1:35.

questions.stem: The minute hand is exactly 15 minute divisions ahead of the hour hand at some instant. What is their angular separation?
questions.explanation: Each minute division is 6°. Fifteen divisions correspond to 15×6° = 90°.

questions.stem: The hands of a correct clock are interchanged at a certain instant between 4 and 5, and the resulting positions correspond to a valid time between 8 and 9. How many minutes after 4 was the original instant?
questions.explanation: Let the original and swapped readings be 4:m and 8:n. The equations are 6m=240+0.5n and 120+0.5m=6n. Solving yields m=6000/143=41 137/143 minutes.

questions.stem: In an ordinary (non-leap) year, a clock is correct at noon on 1 January. It gains uniformly and is exactly 10 minutes fast at noon on 6 January. When will it first be 12 hours fast?
questions.explanation: The clock gains 10 minutes in 5 days, or 2 minutes per day. To gain 720 minutes it needs 720/2 = 360 days from noon on 1 January, which is noon on 27 December of an ordinary year.

questions.stem: At the earlier of two instants between 4:00 and 5:00, the numerical value of the smaller angle between the hands (in degrees) equals the number of minutes after 4:00. What is the time?
questions.explanation: For the earlier instant, 120−5.5m=m. Thus 6.5m=120 and m=240/13=18 6/13 minutes.

questions.stem: Ignoring the identical position at 12:00 twelve hours later, can the hour, minute and second hands of an ideal clock all coincide at any other instant during the next 12 hours?
questions.explanation: Hour-minute coincidence times are multiples of 720/11 minutes, while minute-second coincidence times are multiples of 60/59 minutes. Simultaneous equality requires an integer solution that, within one 12-hour cycle, occurs only at the endpoints. Thus there is no other instant.

questions.stem:
What is the exact time between 2:00 and 3:00?

**Statement I:** The smaller angle between the hands is 50°.

**Statement II:** The minute hand is ahead of the hour hand.
questions.explanation: Statement I yields two candidate times from |60−5.5m|=50. Statement II selects the solution after the hands have crossed, so the exact time is determined only by using both statements.

options.label: Statement I alone is sufficient, but Statement II alone is not sufficient.
Both statements together are sufficient, but neither statement alone is sufficient.
Statement II alone is sufficient, but Statement I alone is not sufficient.
Even both statements together are not sufficient.

questions.stem: Clock A gains 3 minutes every 8 hours, while Clock B loses 5 minutes every 12 hours. Starting together, after how many actual hours will their readings differ by 55 minutes?
questions.explanation: A gains 3/8 minute per hour; B loses 5/12 minute per hour. Relative divergence = 3/8+5/12 = 19/24 minute per hour. Required time = 55÷(19/24) = 1320/19 hours ≈ 69.4737 hours.

questions.stem: Three alert bells ring every 20 seconds, 30 seconds and 45 seconds. They ring together at time zero. During the next 30 minutes, excluding time zero but including the endpoint, how many more times do all three ring together?
questions.explanation: LCM(20,30,45)=180 seconds. Thirty minutes is 1,800 seconds, so joint rings occur at 180,360,…,1800: 10 times.

questions.stem: A clock’s hour hand moves normally, but its minute hand moves 20% faster than normal. Both hands are together at noon. At what actual time do they next coincide?
questions.explanation: The fast minute hand moves at 7.2° per minute; the hour hand moves at 0.5° per minute. Relative speed is 6.7° per minute. Time to gain 360° is 360/6.7 = 3600/67 = 53 49/67 minutes.

questions.stem: A student invests ₹20,000 at 10% compound interest, compounded annually, for 2 years. What is the maturity amount?
A college endowment places ₹50,000 at 8% compound interest for 3 years. How much compound interest is earned?
An annual-compounding deposit grows to ₹30,250 in 2 years at 10%. What was the principal?
An investment becomes 121% of its original value in 2 years under annual compounding. What is the annual rate?
A workstation worth ₹80,000 depreciates by 10% each year. What is its value after 3 years?
What is the effective two-year growth on an amount compounded annually at 6%?
questions.explanation: Two-year multiplier = 1.06² = 1.1236, so growth = 12.36%.

questions.stem: A lab reserve of ₹16,000 grows at 5% compounded annually. What is its value after 4 years?
A server costing ₹1,00,000 loses 8% of its value annually. What is its book value after 2 years?
A user base grows by 12% in each of three years. What is the overall percentage growth?
₹25,000 is invested for 2 years at 8% per annum compounded half-yearly. Find the amount.
questions.explanation: Half-year rate is 4% and there are 4 periods. Amount = 25,000(1.04)^4 = ₹29,246.46.

questions.stem: What effective annual rate corresponds to a nominal 12% rate compounded quarterly?
questions.explanation: Quarterly rate = 3%. Effective annual rate = [(1.03)^4−1]×100 = 12.5509%.

questions.stem: A technology fund earns 10%, 8%, and 12% in three successive years. What is the final value of ₹40,000?
questions.explanation: Varying annual rates compound multiplicatively: 40,000×1.10×1.08×1.12 = ₹53,222.40.

questions.stem: An investment grows by 25% over 3 years with a constant annual compound rate. What is the approximate annual rate?
A drone valued at ₹36,000 depreciates by 15% in the first year and 10% in the second. What is its value after two years?
For ₹25,000 at 12% per annum for 2 years, by how much does annual compound interest exceed simple interest?
A sum amounts to ₹13,310 in 3 years at 10% compounded annually. Find the original sum.
₹60,000 earns 9% in each of the first two years and 11% in the third, with annual compounding. What is the amount?
A battery retains 80% of its capacity each year. What percentage of its initial capacity remains after 3 years?
questions.explanation: Retained fraction = 0.8³ = 0.512, or 51.2%.

questions.stem: How much compound interest is earned on ₹50,000 for 3 years at 10% per annum compounded half-yearly?
A machine’s replacement cost rises from ₹5,00,000 to ₹6,05,000 in 2 years. Assuming constant annual compounding, what is the inflation rate?
questions.explanation: Growth factor = 6.05/5 = 1.21. Annual factor = √1.21 = 1.10, so the rate is 10%.

questions.stem: How much must be deposited today at 8% annual compounding to have ₹1,00,000 after 3 years?
₹30,000 is invested for 18 months at 12% per annum compounded quarterly. What amount is received?
questions.explanation: Quarterly rate = 3%; 18 months gives 6 quarters. Amount = 30,000(1.03)^6 = ₹35,821.57.

questions.stem: A town of 2,00,000 people loses 5% of its population in one year, then grows by 4% in each of the next two years. What is the resulting population?
On ₹45,000 for 2 years, annual compound interest exceeds simple interest by ₹405. What is the annual rate?
questions.explanation: For two years, difference = P(r/100)². Thus (r/100)²=405/45,000=0.009, so r=9.4868%.

questions.stem: At 10% annual compounding, an account balance is ₹24,200 at the end of year 2. How much interest is credited during year 3?
questions.explanation: Third-year interest is 10% of the opening third-year balance: 0.10×24,200 = ₹2,420.

questions.stem:
What is the annual compound-interest rate?

**Statement I:** A sum becomes 1.21 times itself in 2 years.

**Statement II:** The compound interest on ₹10,000 for 2 years is ₹2,100.
questions.explanation: Either statement gives the two-year growth factor 1.21, hence (1+r)^2=1.21 and r=10%. Each alone is sufficient.

options.label: Both statements together are sufficient, but neither statement alone is sufficient.
Even both statements together are not sufficient.
Statement I alone is sufficient, but Statement II alone is not sufficient.
Statement II alone is sufficient, but Statement I alone is not sufficient.

questions.stem: For ₹20,000 at 10% for 3 years, by how much does compound interest exceed simple interest?
What principal at 12% compounded annually for 2 years will equal the maturity value of ₹50,000 at 8% for 3 years?
questions.explanation: Required principal P satisfies P(1.12)²=50,000(1.08)³. Hence P=₹50,211.73.

questions.stem: A machine worth ₹1,20,000 depreciates by 12% annually for 2 years. A retrofit then raises its current value by 25%. What is the post-retrofit value?
questions.explanation: After depreciation: 1,20,000×0.88². Retrofit multiplies that by 1.25. Value = ₹1,16,160.

questions.stem: At 10% annual compounding, after how many years does an investment exactly double according to logarithmic interpolation?
questions.explanation: Solve (1.10)^t=2. Thus t=log 2/log 1.10=7.2725 years.

questions.stem: On ₹1,00,000 for one year, how much more is earned at 10% compounded half-yearly than at 10% compounded annually?
questions.explanation: Half-yearly amount = 1,00,000(1.05)²=₹1,10,250; annual amount=₹1,10,000. Difference=₹250.

questions.stem: An investment earns r% in the first year and (r+2)% in the second. Its two-year compound growth is 20.9%. Find r.
questions.explanation: Let r be decimal. (1+r)(1+r+0.02)=1.209. The positive solution is r=0.09, so r=9%.

questions.stem: A loan is repaid by two equal instalments of ₹12,100 at the ends of years 1 and 2. At 10% annual compound interest, what was the loan amount?
A ₹50,000 loan bears 10% compound interest. A payment of ₹10,000 is made at the end of year 1. What balance remains at the end of year 2 before any second payment?
₹10,000 is deposited at the end of each of three years into an account earning 10% annually. What is the balance immediately after the third deposit?
questions.explanation: The deposits grow for 2, 1, and 0 years: 10,000(1.10²+1.10+1)=₹33,100.

questions.stem: An account starts with ₹40,000 and earns 8% annually. ₹10,000 is withdrawn at each year-end for two years, after interest is credited. What balance remains after the second withdrawal?
For the same nominal rate of 12%, by how many percentage points does quarterly compounding exceed half-yearly compounding over one year?
questions.explanation: Quarterly effective rate = 12.5509%; half-yearly = 12.36%. Difference = 0.190881 percentage point.

questions.stem: The interest credited in years 2 and 3 of an annually compounded investment is ₹5,500 and ₹6,050 respectively. What was the original principal?
questions.explanation: Successive yearly interests grow by factor 6,050/5,500=1.10, so rate=10%. The balance entering year 2 is 5,500/0.10=₹55,000, which equals 1.10P. Thus P=₹50,000.

questions.stem: A campus town grows by 10% annually and reaches 2,66,200 after 3 years. What was its population three years earlier?
A sensor retains 90% of accuracy after each of its first two calibration cycles and 95% after each of the next three. What percentage of its original accuracy remains?

What is the principal under annual compounding?

**Statement I:** The amount after 2 years is ₹48,400.

**Statement II:** The first-year interest is ₹4,000 and the second-year interest is ₹4,400.
questions.explanation: Statement I alone lacks the rate. Statement II gives second/first interest =1.10, so rate=10%; principal=4,000/0.10=₹40,000. Statement II alone is sufficient.

options.label: Both statements together are sufficient, but neither statement alone is sufficient.
Even both statements together are not sufficient.
Statement II alone is sufficient, but Statement I alone is not sufficient.
Statement I alone is sufficient, but Statement II alone is not sufficient.

questions.stem: On ₹80,000 for 2 years at a nominal 8%, how much more does quarterly compounding produce than annual compounding?
questions.explanation: Quarterly amount = 80,000(1.02)^8; annual amount = 80,000(1.08)^2. Their difference is ₹420.75 (approximately).

questions.stem: For an annual-compounding investment, the amount after 5 years is 1.331 times the amount after 2 years. What is the annual rate?
questions.explanation: The ratio removes the first two years: (1+r)^3=1.331=1.1³. Hence r=10%.

questions.stem: At 10% annual compounding, a loan is repaid by ₹11,000 after 1 year, ₹12,100 after 2 years, and ₹13,310 after 3 years. What was the loan principal?
A fund gains 10% in year 1, loses x% in year 2, and gains 20% in year 3. Its overall three-year gain is 18.8%. Find x.
A ₹30,000 loan at 10% annual compounding is to be cleared by three equal year-end payments. What should each payment be?
questions.explanation: If payment is X, present value is X(1/1.1+1/1.1²+1/1.1³)=30,000. Thus X=₹12,063.44.

questions.stem: What balance enters Year 2 after the withdrawal?
questions.explanation: Year-1 closing value before withdrawal is ₹11,20,000. After withdrawing ₹2,00,000, ₹9,20,000 enters Year 2.

questions.stem: What is the balance at the end of Year 2?
What is the fund balance at the end of Year 3?
Ignoring the timing of the withdrawal and comparing total value received (final balance plus withdrawal) with the initial investment, what is the overall percentage gain?
A sensor reports 0.375 of its full-scale range. Express 0.375 as a fraction in lowest terms.
questions.explanation: 0.375 = 375/1000. Dividing numerator and denominator by 125 gives 3/8.

questions.stem: What is the decimal representation of 7/16?
questions.explanation: Since 1/16 = 0.0625, multiplying by 7 gives 7/16 = 0.4375.

questions.stem: Which of the following numbers is the greatest?
questions.explanation: Write all numbers to four decimal places: 0.6200, 0.6020, 0.6220 and 0.6199. Hence 0.622 is greatest.

questions.stem: A debugging session lasts 12.75 minutes and a verification step lasts 3.086 minutes. What is their combined duration?
questions.explanation: Align the decimal points: 12.750 + 3.086 = 15.836 minutes.

questions.stem: A 50 GB allocation has 18.625 GB in use. How many gigabytes remain?
questions.explanation: Remaining capacity = 50.000 − 18.625 = 31.375 GB.

questions.stem: Evaluate 0.24 × 0.35.
questions.explanation: 24 × 35 = 840. The two factors contain four decimal places in total, so the product is 0.084.

questions.stem: A 4.8-litre solution is packed equally into containers of 0.06 litre each. How many containers are filled?
In the number 13.4075, what is the place value of the digit 7?
questions.explanation: The digits after the decimal are tenths, hundredths, thousandths and ten-thousandths. Thus 7 represents 7 thousandths, or 0.007.

questions.stem: Round 8.4763 to two decimal places.
questions.explanation: The third decimal digit is 6, so the hundredths digit 7 is increased to 8. The rounded value is 8.48.

questions.stem: The decimal 0.3333… repeats indefinitely. What fraction does it represent?
questions.explanation: Let x = 0.3333…. Then 10x − x = 3, so 9x = 3 and x = 1/3.

questions.stem: A calibration constant is 0.00725. If the decimal point is shifted three places to the right, what is the new value?
questions.explanation: Shifting three places right multiplies by 1000: 0.00725 × 1000 = 7.25.
The numerator is 2.76. Multiplying numerator and divisor by 100 gives 276 ÷ 12 = 23.

questions.stem: A test vehicle travels 18.6 km using 1.24 litres of fuel. At the same rate, how many kilometres does it travel per litre?
questions.explanation: Mileage = 18.6/1.24. Multiplying both by 100 gives 1860/124 = 15 km per litre.

questions.stem: A component weighs 2.375 kg. What is its weight in grams?
questions.explanation: One kilogram is 1000 grams, so 2.375 × 1000 = 2375 grams.

questions.stem: Which fraction has a terminating decimal expansion?
questions.explanation: After reduction, a fraction terminates exactly when its denominator has no prime factors other than 2 and 5. The denominator 40 = 2³ × 5 meets this condition; 18, 21 and 45 leave a factor 3 or 7.

questions.stem: Without carrying out the multiplication, how many digits will appear after the decimal point in 0.0025 × 0.036?
questions.explanation: The first factor has four decimal places and the second has three. The raw product has seven places: 25 × 36 = 900, giving 0.0000900. Ignoring trailing zero notation, the value is 0.00009, whose first nonzero digit is at the fifth decimal place.

questions.stem: A software licence priced at ₹4,800 is discounted by 0.125 of its price. What amount is payable before tax?
questions.explanation: 0.125 = 1/8. The discount is ₹600, so the payable amount is ₹4,200.

questions.stem: Convert the recurring decimal 0.272727… to a fraction in lowest terms.
Four latency measurements are 4.75 ms, 5.08 ms, 6.125 ms and 4.045 ms. What is their arithmetic mean?
questions.explanation: Their sum is 20.000 ms. Dividing by 4 gives a mean of 5 ms.

questions.stem: Simplify the ratio 0.84 : 1.26.
questions.explanation: Multiplying both terms by 100 gives 84:126. Dividing by 42 yields 2:3.

questions.stem: If 0.7x + 1.4 = 5.6, what is x?
questions.explanation: Subtracting 1.4 gives 0.7x = 4.2. Thus x = 4.2/0.7 = 6.

questions.stem: Which scientific-notation form is equal to 0.0000458?
questions.explanation: Move the decimal five places right to obtain 4.58, so the multiplier is 10⁻⁵.

questions.stem: A technician enters 3.6 instead of 0.36 in a calculation. By what percentage does the entered value exceed the intended value?
questions.explanation: The excess is 3.24. Relative to 0.36, the excess percentage is 3.24/0.36 × 100 = 900%.

questions.stem:
Is the positive decimal number x greater than 0.5?

**Statement I:** 4x > 1.8.

**Statement II:** 3x < 1.8.
questions.explanation: Statement I gives x > 0.45, which does not decide whether x exceeds 0.5. Statement II gives x < 0.6, also insufficient. Together, 0.45 < x < 0.6, which still includes values on both sides of 0.5. Even together they are insufficient.

options.label: Statement II alone is sufficient, but Statement I alone is not sufficient.
Both statements together are sufficient, but neither statement alone is sufficient.
Even both statements together are not sufficient.
Statement I alone is sufficient, but Statement II alone is not sufficient.

questions.stem: When 7.35 is divided into the greatest possible number of complete portions of size 0.4, what quotient and remainder result?
questions.explanation: Eighteen complete portions use 18 × 0.4 = 7.2, leaving 7.35 − 7.2 = 0.15.
1.44/0.12 = 12 and 0.875/0.025 = 35. Their sum is 47; dividing by 0.5 doubles it to 94.

questions.stem: Express 0.123123123… as a fraction in lowest terms.
Which of the following decimals lies strictly between 7/20 and 9/25?
questions.explanation: 7/20 = 0.35 and 9/25 = 0.36. Among the options, only 0.357 lies strictly between them.

questions.stem: A fault occurs in 0.00072 of transactions, while a warning is triggered in 0.018 of transactions. The fault rate is what fraction of the warning rate?
The decimal expansion of 1/13 is 0.076923076923…. What is the 2026th digit after the decimal point?
questions.explanation: The repeating block 076923 has length 6. Since 2026 leaves remainder 4 when divided by 6, the required digit is the fourth digit of the block, namely 9.

questions.stem: Three data batches contain 120, 180 and 100 GB. Their usable fractions are 0.84, 0.91 and 0.775, respectively. What fraction of the combined data is usable?
A positive quantity is recorded as 18.47 after rounding to two decimal places. Which interval must contain the exact quantity?
questions.explanation: Rounding to 18.47 means the exact value is at least 18.465 and strictly less than 18.475.

questions.stem: Compute 0.0048 × 0.00035 and express the result as an ordinary decimal.
questions.explanation: 48 × 35 = 1680. There are 4 + 5 = 9 decimal places before removing the trailing zero, so the value is 0.00000168.

questions.stem: If x = 0.181818… and y = 0.05555…, what is x − y?
How many fractions of the form k/200, where 1 ≤ k ≤ 199, have terminating decimal expansions in lowest terms?
questions.explanation: Since 200 = 2³×5², every denominator obtained after reducing k/200 contains only factors 2 and 5. Therefore all 199 positive proper fractions terminate.

questions.stem: Evaluate 0.125 + 0.0125 + 0.00125 + 0.000125 exactly as a fraction.
The reciprocals of two positive decimals are not required separately. If their sum is 0.25 and one of them is 0.20, what is the reciprocal of their sum?
questions.explanation: The sum is already 0.25, so its reciprocal is 1/0.25 = 4. The stated individual value is irrelevant.

questions.stem:
Does the reduced fraction representing a positive rational number r have a terminating decimal expansion?

**Statement I:** r = a/40 for some integer a.

**Statement II:** 24r is an integer.
questions.explanation: Statement I is sufficient: after reduction, the denominator divides 40 = 2³×5, so the decimal terminates. Statement II is not sufficient because 24r can be an integer for both r = 1/3 (nonterminating) and r = 1/8 (terminating). Thus Statement I alone is sufficient.

options.label: Statement I alone is sufficient, but Statement II alone is not sufficient.
Statement II alone is sufficient, but Statement I alone is not sufficient.
Both statements together are sufficient, but neither statement alone is sufficient.
Even both statements together are not sufficient.

questions.stem: What is the compressed size of reading A?
What is the total compressed size of the three readings?
questions.explanation: Compressed sizes are 0.546875, 1.1 and 0.0875 MB. Their sum is 1.734375 MB.

questions.stem: How many megabytes are saved by compression?
questions.explanation: Original total = 2.0875 MB. Compressed total = 1.734375 MB. Saving = 0.353125 MB.

questions.stem: Convert 0.12̅3̅, in which the block 23 repeats after the initial digit 1 (that is, 0.1232323…), to a fraction.
A measurement rounded to three decimal places is 7.326. A second measurement rounded to two decimal places is 2.41. What is the smallest possible value of their exact difference?
questions.explanation: The first exact value lies in [7.3255, 7.3265), and the second in [2.405, 2.415). To minimize the positive difference, take the first at its minimum and the second arbitrarily close to its maximum: the infimum is 7.3255 − 2.415 = 4.9105. It is approached but not attained.

options.label: Greater than 4.9105 but arbitrarily close to it

questions.stem: The decimal expansion of 1/7 is 0.142857142857…. What is the sum of the digits in positions 1001 through 1012 after the decimal point?
questions.explanation: The repeating block has six digits with sum 1+4+2+8+5+7 = 27. Twelve consecutive positions cover exactly two full blocks, regardless of starting point. The required sum is 2×27 = 54.

questions.stem: A positive number x satisfies 0.0̅6̅ × x = 1.2, where 0.0̅6̅ means 0.0565656…. Find x.
For how many integers n with 1 ≤ n ≤ 1000 does n/360 have a terminating decimal expansion after reduction?
questions.explanation: Since 360 = 2³×3²×5, the reduced denominator must lose both factors of 3. Thus n must be divisible by 9. There are floor(1000/9) = 111 such integers.

questions.stem: Which interval contains every possible exact value of x?
questions.explanation: A display of 2.73 to two decimal places means 2.725 ≤ x < 2.735.

questions.stem: Before rounding y, which interval must contain its exact value?
questions.explanation: Because reciprocal is decreasing for positive values, 1/2.735 < y ≤ 1/2.725. Numerically this is approximately 0.3656307 < y ≤ 0.3669725.

questions.stem: How many distinct four-decimal-place values can the display for y possibly show?
questions.explanation: The interval for y runs from just above 0.3656307 to 0.3669725 inclusive. Rounding to four decimals can produce 0.3656 through 0.3670. These are 15 values: 0.3656, 0.3657, …, 0.3670.

questions.stem: Find the HCF of 48 and 72.
questions.explanation: 48=2⁴×3 and 72=2³×3². Taking the smaller exponents gives 2³×3=24.

questions.stem: Find the LCM of 12 and 18.
questions.explanation: 12=2²×3 and 18=2×3². Taking the larger exponents gives 2²×3²=36.

questions.stem: What is the greatest length that can measure exactly both 84 cm and 126 cm?
questions.explanation: The greatest exact measuring length is HCF(84,126)=42 cm.

questions.stem: What is the least positive number divisible by both 8 and 10?
questions.explanation: The required number is LCM(8,10)=40.

questions.stem: Which pair is coprime?
questions.explanation: The HCF of 14 and 25 is 1. The other pairs share factors 2, 3 and 7 respectively.

questions.stem: Three alarms ring every 4, 6 and 8 minutes. If they ring together now, after how many minutes will they next ring together?
questions.explanation: They next coincide after LCM(4,6,8)=24 minutes.

questions.stem: How many common positive factors do 24 and 36 have?
questions.explanation: Their HCF is 12. The positive factors of 12 are 1,2,3,4,6,12, so there are 6 common factors.

questions.stem: If the HCF of two numbers is 5, which of the following must divide both numbers?
questions.explanation: By definition, the HCF divides each number. Therefore 5 must divide both.

questions.stem: A dual-counter pattern resets every 7 steps on one counter and every 9 steps on the other. After how many steps do both counters reset together for the first time?
questions.explanation: The first common reset occurs after LCM(7,9). Since the cycle lengths are coprime, this is 7×9=63 steps.

questions.stem: The HCF of 15 and 25 is multiplied by their LCM. What is the product?
questions.explanation: For two positive integers, HCF×LCM equals their product. Thus 15×25=375.

questions.stem: Find the least positive integer divisible by 8, 12 and 15.
What is the greatest number that divides 187, 233 and 325 leaving the same remainder in each case?
questions.explanation: Such a divisor must divide all pairwise differences: 233−187=46, 325−233=92 and 325−187=138. Their HCF is 46.

questions.stem: Two numbers have HCF 12 and LCM 420. If one number is 60, what is the other?
questions.explanation: Product of numbers = HCF×LCM = 12×420. The other number is (12×420)/60 = 84.

questions.stem: Find the HCF of the fractions 3/4, 9/10 and 21/25.
questions.explanation: HCF of fractions = HCF of numerators / LCM of denominators. HCF(3,9,21)=3 and LCM(4,10,25)=100, so the HCF is 3/100.

questions.stem: Find the LCM of the fractions 2/9, 5/12 and 7/18.
questions.explanation: LCM of fractions = LCM of numerators / HCF of denominators. LCM(2,5,7)=70 and HCF(9,12,18)=3, so the LCM is 70/3.

questions.stem: A warehouse has 96 routers, 144 switches and 240 access points. It wants the greatest possible number of identical kits with no item left over. How many kits can it make?
questions.explanation: The number of identical kits is HCF(96,144,240)=48.

questions.stem: Buses leave a terminal every 18, 24 and 30 minutes. If all leave together at 7:00 a.m., when will they next leave together?
questions.explanation: LCM(18,24,30)=360 minutes=6 hours. The next common departure is at 1:00 p.m.

questions.stem: Two gears have 24 and 36 teeth. Starting from a marked contact pair, after how many tooth engagements will the same pair meet again?
questions.explanation: The same marked teeth meet after LCM(24,36)=72 engagements.

questions.stem: What is the smallest four-digit number divisible by 8, 9 and 12?
questions.explanation: LCM(8,9,12)=72. The first multiple of 72 at least 1000 is 72×14=1008.

questions.stem: A rectangular floor is 8.4 m by 6.3 m. What is the largest possible side of a square tile, in metres, that covers it exactly?
questions.explanation: Convert to decimetres: 84 dm and 63 dm. Their HCF is 21 dm=2.1 m.

questions.stem: Two numbers are in the ratio 5:7 and their HCF is 9. What are the numbers?
questions.explanation: Because 5 and 7 are coprime, the numbers are 9×5=45 and 9×7=63.

questions.stem: What is the greatest number that divides 122 and 170 leaving remainders 2 and 10, respectively?
questions.explanation: Subtract the remainders: the divisor must divide 120 and 160. Their HCF is 40.

questions.stem: Find the least number which, when divided by 6, 8 and 10, leaves remainder 3 in each case.
questions.explanation: Subtracting 3 gives a multiple of LCM(6,8,10)=120. The least number greater than the divisors is 120+3=123.

questions.stem: The HCF of two numbers is 8 and their product is 1536. If one number is 48, what is their LCM?
questions.explanation: LCM = product/HCF = 1536/8 = 192. The given individual number is a consistency check.

questions.stem:
What is the LCM of positive integers a and b?

**Statement I:** Their HCF is 6 and their product is 540.

**Statement II:** One of the integers is 30.
questions.explanation: Statement I alone gives LCM=product/HCF=540/6=90, so it is sufficient. Statement II alone is not sufficient. Thus Statement I alone is sufficient.

options.label: Even both statements together are not sufficient.
Both statements together are sufficient, but neither statement alone is sufficient.
Statement II alone is sufficient, but Statement I alone is not sufficient.
Statement I alone is sufficient, but Statement II alone is not sufficient.

questions.stem: A class can be arranged in rows of 12, 18 or 24 students with no one left over. What is the least possible class strength?
questions.explanation: The least possible strength is LCM(12,18,24)=72.

questions.stem: Three positive integers have pairwise HCFs 2, 3 and 5. What is the least possible value of their common LCM?
questions.explanation: The numbers 6, 10 and 15 have pairwise HCFs 2, 3 and 5 and common LCM 30. Any valid set must collectively contain the primes 2,3 and5, so its LCM cannot be below 30. Thus 30 is least.

questions.stem: Find the least positive number that leaves remainders 5, 9 and 12 when divided by 8, 12 and 15, respectively.
questions.explanation: Each remainder is three less than the divisor, so n+3 is divisible by 8,12,15. Their LCM is 120, giving n=117.

questions.stem: Find the HCF of 2¹²×3⁵×5² and 2⁸×3⁷×5⁴.
questions.explanation: Take the smaller exponent of each prime: 2⁸×3⁵×5² = 1,555,200.

questions.stem: What is the LCM of 2⁴×3²×7 and 2⁶×3×5²?
questions.explanation: Take maximum prime exponents: 2⁶×3²×5²×7.

questions.stem: How many unordered pairs of positive integers have HCF 6 and LCM 180?
questions.explanation: Write numbers as 6x and 6y with gcd(x,y)=1 and xy=180/6=30. Since 30=2×3×5 has 3 distinct prime factors, distributing whole prime powers between coprime x,y gives 2³ ordered assignments, or 2²=4 unordered pairs.

questions.stem: Find the HCF of 0.84, 1.26 and 2.10.
questions.explanation: Multiply all by 100: HCF(84,126,210)=42. Divide by 100 to obtain 0.42.

questions.stem: Three rods of lengths 7.2 m, 9.6 m and 12 m are cut into equal longest pieces. How many pieces result?
questions.explanation: In decimetres the lengths are 72,96,120; HCF=24 dm=2.4 m. Piece counts are 3,4,5, totaling 12.

questions.stem: A server health check runs every 42 seconds, a log flush every 70 seconds and a backup marker every 90 seconds. If all occur together now, how many minutes pass before the next coincidence?
Two numbers have HCF 14 and LCM 840. If their sum is 266, what is the larger number?
questions.explanation: Let numbers be 14x and 14y with gcd(x,y)=1. Then xy=840/14=60 and x+y=266/14=19. The coprime factor pair of 60 with sum 19 is 4 and 15. Numbers are 56 and 210; larger is 210.

questions.stem: What is the least number of square tiles needed to cover a 15 m by 9 m rectangle without cutting any tile?
questions.explanation: Largest square side = HCF(15,9)=3 m. Number of tiles = (15/3)(9/3)=5×3=15.

questions.stem:
What is the HCF of two positive integers?

**Statement I:** Their ratio in lowest terms is 7:11.

**Statement II:** Their LCM is 462.
questions.explanation: Statement I alone gives only the ratio. Statement II alone allows many pairs. Together the numbers are 7k and 11k, and their LCM is 77k=462, so k=6, which is their HCF. Both together are sufficient.

options.label: Statement II alone is sufficient, but Statement I alone is not sufficient.
Statement I alone is sufficient, but Statement II alone is not sufficient.
Even both statements together are not sufficient.
Both statements together are sufficient, but neither statement alone is sufficient.

questions.stem: After how many days will all three machines next be serviced together?
During the first 180 days after 1 January, excluding 1 January but including day 180, how many times are A and B serviced together?
questions.explanation: A and B coincide every LCM(18,30)=90 days, at days 90 and 180. Hence they coincide twice.

questions.stem: What is the first positive day on which B and C are serviced together but A is not?
questions.explanation: B and C coincide every LCM(30,45)=90 days. But 90 is also a multiple of 18, so A is serviced too; every later B-C coincidence is a multiple of 90 and therefore of 18. Such a day never occurs.

questions.stem: How many services in total occur on day 270?
questions.explanation: 270 is divisible by 18,30 and45, so all three machines are serviced. Total services =3.

questions.stem: The HCF of three numbers is 12 and their LCM is 720. Which of the following cannot be one of the numbers?
questions.explanation: Every number must divide the LCM and be a multiple of the HCF. 180,240 and360 satisfy both. 420 does not divide 720, so it cannot be one of the numbers.

questions.stem: Two positive integers have HCF 12, LCM 720 and sum 204. What is their positive difference?
questions.explanation: Write them as 12x,12y with gcd(x,y)=1. Then xy=60 and x+y=17. The coprime factor pair is 5,12, so numbers are 60 and144. Difference=84.

questions.stem: What is the smallest positive integer n such that LCM(1,2,…,n) is divisible by 2⁵×3³×5²×7?
questions.explanation: The LCM through n contains the largest prime powers not exceeding n. To include 2⁵=32, 3³=27, 5²=25 and 7, n must be at least max(32,27,25,7)=32. At n=32 all are present.

questions.stem: A distributor has 252 red, 198 blue and 144 green units. It must create identical nonempty packs using all units, with each pack containing at least two units of every colour. What is the greatest possible number of packs?
questions.explanation: The unconstrained maximum is HCF(252,198,144)=18. Each pack then has 14 red,11 blue and8 green, meeting the minimum. Therefore 18 packs are possible.

questions.stem: For positive integer n, what is HCF(n²+n, n²+3n+2)?
questions.explanation: Factor: n²+n=n(n+1) and n²+3n+2=(n+1)(n+2). Their HCF is (n+1)×HCF(n,n+2). This equals n+1 when n is odd and 2(n+1) when n is even.

options.label: n+1 if n is odd; 2(n+1) if n is even
2(n+1) if n is odd; n+1 if n is even

questions.stem: What is H?
questions.explanation: Take minimum exponents across A,B,C: 2³×3¹, while 5 and7 have minimum exponent zero. Hence H=24.

questions.stem: Using the maximum prime exponents in A, B, and C, determine the divisor count of their LCM.
What is L/H?
How many integers divide L and are multiples of H?
questions.explanation: Such integers are H×d where d divides L/H. Since L/H=2²×3³×5²×7, the count is (2+1)(3+1)(2+1)(1+1)=72.

questions.stem: From a point 20 m from the base of a vertical tower, the angle of elevation of its top is 45°. What is the tower’s height?
questions.explanation: tan 45° = height/20 = 1, so the height is 20 m.

questions.stem: A vertical pole casts a 15 m shadow when the sun’s elevation is 45°. Find the pole’s height.
questions.explanation: tan 45° = height/shadow = 1. Therefore height = 15 m.

questions.stem: A pole casts a shadow of length 12√3 m when the sun’s elevation is 30°. What is the pole’s height?
questions.explanation: height = shadow × tan30° = 12√3 × 1/√3 = 12 m.

questions.stem: An observer’s eye is 1.5 m above the ground. From 30√3 m away, the angle of elevation of the top of a building is 30°. What is the building’s height?
questions.explanation: Height above eye level = 30√3×tan30° = 30 m. Adding eye height gives 31.5 m.

questions.stem: A person on a lighthouse sees a boat at an angle of depression of 35°. What is the boat’s angle of elevation to the person?
questions.explanation: The horizontal lines through the observer and the boat are parallel, so the angle of depression equals the angle of elevation: 35°.

questions.stem: A 13 m ladder rests against a vertical wall with its foot 5 m from the wall. How high up the wall does it reach?
questions.explanation: The ladder, wall and ground form a right triangle. Height = √(13²−5²)=√144=12 m.

questions.stem: A tower is 30√3 m high. From what horizontal distance is its angle of elevation 60°?
questions.explanation: tan60° = height/distance = √3. Thus distance = 30√3/√3 = 30 m.

questions.stem: An 8 m pole stands vertically. What is the length of its shadow when the sun’s elevation is 30°?
questions.explanation: shadow = height/tan30° = 8√3 m.

questions.stem: The line joining the tops of two vertical towers is horizontal. What can be concluded?
questions.explanation: A horizontal joining line means the tops are at the same elevation. If both bases are on the same level ground, the towers have equal heights.

options.label: One tower is twice the other
The towers are equally far apart as they are high

questions.stem: A guy wire makes a 60° angle with level ground and supports the top of a 12√3 m mast. How long is the wire?
questions.explanation: If L is the wire length, L sin60°=12√3. Hence L×√3/2=12√3, so L=24 m.

questions.stem: From a point 24 m from a building, an observer whose eye is 1.6 m above the ground sees the roof at 45°. Find the building’s height.
questions.explanation: The roof is 24 m above eye level because tan45°=1. Total height = 24+1.6=25.6 m.

questions.stem: Two observation points lie on the same side of a tower and are 40 m apart. The angles of elevation are 60° at the nearer point and 30° at the farther point. What is the tower’s height?
questions.explanation: Let the nearer distance be x. Then h=x√3 and h=(x+40)/√3. Hence 3x=x+40, so x=20 and h=20√3 m.

questions.stem: From the top of a 60 m lighthouse, the angle of depression of a boat is 30°. How far is the boat from the lighthouse base?
A 20 m pole casts a shadow when the sun’s elevation is 45°. Later the elevation becomes 30°. By how much does the shadow length increase?
questions.explanation: At 45°, shadow=20 m. At 30°, shadow=20√3 m. Increase=20(√3−1) m.

questions.stem: From a point 40 m from a building, the angle to the roof is 45° and the angle to the top of an antenna mounted on the roof is 60°. Find the antenna’s height.
questions.explanation: Building height=40 m. Total height=40√3 m. Antenna height=40(√3−1) m.

questions.stem: A straight access ramp is 50 m long and inclined at 30° to the horizontal. What vertical height does it gain?
questions.explanation: Vertical rise = 50 sin30° = 25 m.

questions.stem: A drone is observed at an elevation angle of 60° from a point 150 m horizontally from the point directly below it. What is the drone’s altitude?
questions.explanation: Altitude=150 tan60°=150√3 m.

questions.stem: An observer stands between two vertical poles. One pole is 20√3 m high and appears at 60° elevation; the other is 20 m high and appears at 45°. How far apart are the poles?
questions.explanation: The observer is 20 m from the first pole and 20 m from the second. Since the poles are on opposite sides, their separation is 40 m.

questions.stem: From a point on one bank of a river, the top of a tree directly opposite on the other bank is seen at 45°. The tree is 30 m high. What is the river’s width?
questions.explanation: tan45°=30/width=1, so width=30 m.

questions.stem: From the top of a 50 m tower, a car on level ground is seen at a depression angle of 45°. How far is the car from the tower base?
questions.explanation: The car’s angle of elevation is 45°. Thus horizontal distance=50/tan45°=50 m.

questions.stem: From the roof of a 30 m building, the top of another building 30√3 m away is seen at 30° elevation. What is the second building’s height?
questions.explanation: Height difference=30√3 tan30°=30 m. The second building is 30+30=60 m high.

questions.stem:
What is the height of a vertical tower on level ground?

**Statement I:** From a point 50 m from its base, the angle of elevation is 45°.

**Statement II:** The tower casts a 50 m shadow when the sun’s elevation is 45°.
questions.explanation: Statement I gives height=50 tan45°=50 m. Statement II independently gives height=50 tan45°=50 m. Each statement alone is sufficient.

options.label: Statement II alone is sufficient, but Statement I alone is not sufficient.
Even both statements together are not sufficient.
Statement I alone is sufficient, but Statement II alone is not sufficient.
Both statements together are sufficient, but neither statement alone is sufficient.

questions.stem: An inclinometer at a student’s eye level, 1.5 m above ground, reads 45° to the top of a pole 10 m away. What is the pole’s height?
questions.explanation: Height above eye level=10 tan45°=10 m. Total height=11.5 m.

questions.stem: From a point 30 m from a building, the roof is seen at 45° and the top of a flagpole on the roof at 60°. What is the flagpole’s height?
questions.explanation: Roof height=30 m; total height=30√3 m. Flagpole height=30(√3−1) m.

questions.stem: Two points on the same straight road are 25 m apart. The nearer point sees the top of a tower at 45°, and the farther point at 30°. What is the tower’s height?
questions.explanation: Let the nearer distance and height be h. At the farther point, tan30°=h/(h+25). Thus √3h=h+25, so h=25/(√3−1)=25(√3+1)/2 m.

questions.stem: A person walks 40 m toward a tower. The angle of elevation changes from 30° to 60°. Find the tower’s height.
questions.explanation: Let the initial distance be x. Then h=x/√3=(x−40)√3. Hence x=60 and h=20√3 m.

questions.stem: Two observers are on opposite sides of a tower, 100 m apart. Their elevation angles to the top are 30° and 45°. What is the tower’s height?
questions.explanation: Let distances from the tower be x and y, with x+y=100. From the 30° side, h=x/√3; from the 45° side, h=y. Thus x=√3y and y(1+√3)=100, giving h=50(√3−1) m.

questions.stem: A tower stands between two points 70 m apart. Its elevation angles from the points are 45° and 30°. What is the tower’s height?
questions.explanation: Let the distance from the 45° point be h. The other distance is 70−h and tan30°=h/(70−h). Thus √3h=70−h, giving h=35(√3−1) m.

questions.stem: From a point 50 m from a building, the roof is seen at 30° and the top of a mast on the roof at 45°. Find the mast’s height.
questions.explanation: Building height=50/√3. Total height=50. Mast height=50−50/√3=50(√3−1)/√3 m.

questions.stem: From the top of an 80 m cliff, a boat is first seen at 30° depression. It sails straight toward the cliff until the depression is 45°. How far does it travel?
questions.explanation: Initial distance=80√3 m; final distance=80 m. Travel=80(√3−1) m.

questions.stem: Two balloons lie on the same vertical line. From a ground point their elevation angles are 30° and 60°, and their vertical separation is 80√3 m. How far is the point from the vertical line?
questions.explanation: If horizontal distance is d, the heights are d/√3 and d√3. Their difference is 2d/√3=80√3, so 2d=240 and d=120 m.

questions.stem: From the top of a 90 m tower, two cars on the same side are seen at depression angles of 30° and 60°. What is the distance between the cars?
questions.explanation: Their distances from the tower are 90√3 and 30√3 m. Difference=60√3 m.

questions.stem: A train moves directly toward a tower at 12 m/s. The elevation angle of the top changes from 30° to 60° in 10 seconds. Find the tower’s height.
questions.explanation: The train covers 120 m. Let initial distance be x. Then x/√3=(x−120)√3, giving x=180. Height=180/√3=60√3 m.

questions.stem: A vertical pole breaks 8 m above the ground, and its top touches the ground 15 m from the base. What was the pole’s original height?
questions.explanation: The broken upper part is the hypotenuse of a right triangle with legs 8 and 15, so its length is 17 m. Original height=8+17=25 m.

questions.stem: From ground level, the top of a hill is seen at 45°. From the top of a 20 m observation tower at the same point, it is seen at 30°. What is the hill’s height above ground?
questions.explanation: Let hill height and horizontal distance both be H from the 45° observation. From the tower, (H−20)/H=tan30°=1/√3. Thus H=20/(1−1/√3)=10(3+√3) m.

questions.stem: An observer is 50 m vertically above the near edge of a canyon. The far edge is at the same ground level and is seen at a depression angle of 30°. What is the canyon’s width?
questions.explanation: tan30°=50/width, so width=50√3 m.

questions.stem: A drone is at coordinates (60, 80, h) metres relative to an observer at the origin. If its elevation angle is 45°, what is h?
questions.explanation: Horizontal distance=√(60²+80²)=100 m. At 45°, altitude equals horizontal distance, so h=100 m.

questions.stem:
What is the height of a tower?

**Statement I:** From point A, its elevation angle is 30°.

**Statement II:** After moving 40 m directly toward the tower, the elevation angle is 60°.
questions.explanation: Neither statement alone provides a scale. Together, if the initial distance is x, h=x/√3=(x−40)√3, which uniquely gives h=20√3 m. Both together are sufficient.

options.label: Even both statements together are not sufficient.
Statement II alone is sufficient, but Statement I alone is not sufficient.
Statement I alone is sufficient, but Statement II alone is not sufficient.
Both statements together are sufficient, but neither statement alone is sufficient.

questions.stem: Two cables run from the top of a 24 m mast to ground anchors on opposite sides, 10 m and 18 m from the base. What total cable length is required?
questions.explanation: Cable lengths are √(24²+10²)=26 m and √(24²+18²)=30 m. Total=56 m.

questions.stem: From the roof of a 40 m building, the base of another building is seen at 30° depression and its top at 45° elevation. Find the other building’s height.
questions.explanation: Horizontal separation=40/tan30°=40√3 m. The top is an additional 40√3 m above the observer. Total height=40+40√3=40(1+√3) m.

questions.stem: Two vertical towers are 30 m and 70 m high and their bases are 40√3 m apart. What angle does the line joining their tops make with the horizontal?
questions.explanation: Vertical difference=40 m. tanθ=40/(40√3)=1/√3, so θ=30°.

questions.stem: A 60 m tower is viewed from a point 60 m east of its base. The observer then moves 80 m north without changing elevation. What is the tangent of the new elevation angle?
questions.explanation: The new horizontal distance from the base is √(60²+80²)=100 m. Therefore tanθ=60/100=3/5.

questions.stem: Observation points A and B lie on two perpendicular ground rays from the base O of a tower. The elevation angle is 45° at A and has tangent 3/4 at B. If AB=50 m, find the tower’s height.
questions.explanation: Let height=h. Then OA=h and OB=4h/3. Since OA⊥OB, AB=√(h²+16h²/9)=5h/3. Thus 5h/3=50 and h=30 m.

questions.stem: A vertical tower stands on a plane inclined at 30° to the horizontal. An observer is 100 m down the line of greatest slope from the base, and the top is seen at 45° above the horizontal. What is the tower’s height?
questions.explanation: The base is horizontally 100cos30°=50√3 m away and vertically 100sin30°=50 m above the observer. A 45° sightline has total vertical rise 50√3 m. Tower height=50√3−50=50(√3−1) m.

questions.stem: A 60 m lighthouse is observed by one ship due east at 30° elevation and another ship due north at 45° elevation. How far apart are the ships?
questions.explanation: The east ship is 60√3 m from the base and the north ship 60 m away. Their paths are perpendicular, so separation=√[(60√3)²+60²]=√14400=120 m.

questions.stem: Two ground sensors A and B are 210 m apart. A drone’s vertical projection lies between them. Its elevation angles are 45° at A and 60° at B. What is the drone’s altitude?
questions.explanation: Let distance from A be x; altitude h=x. From B, h=(210−x)√3. Thus x=(210−x)√3, giving h=x=105(3−√3) m.

questions.stem: Two points on the same side of a tower are 90 m apart. The tangents of their elevation angles are 2 and 1/2, respectively. What is the tower’s height?
questions.explanation: If height=h, the nearer distance is h/2 and the farther distance is 2h. Their difference is 3h/2=90, so h=60 m.

questions.stem: Two towers 20 m and 45 m high stand 70 m apart. A point lies between their bases. The two elevation angles from that point add to 90°. What are the possible distances from the 20 m tower?
questions.explanation: If the distance is x, tanα=20/x and tanβ=45/(70−x). Since α+β=90°, tanα·tanβ=1. Thus x(70−x)=900, giving x²−70x+900=0 and x=35±5√13.

questions.stem:
What is the height of a tower standing on level ground?

**Statement I:** From A, its elevation angle is 45°.

**Statement II:** From B, 30 m farther from the tower along the same line, its elevation angle is 30°.
questions.explanation: Statement I alone gives height equal to distance from A but no scale. Statement II alone also lacks a scale. Together, if height=x, then x/(x+30)=1/√3, so the height is uniquely determined. Both statements together are sufficient.

options.label: Both statements together are sufficient, but neither statement alone is sufficient.
Statement II alone is sufficient, but Statement I alone is not sufficient.
Statement I alone is sufficient, but Statement II alone is not sufficient.
Even both statements together are not sufficient.

questions.stem: A drone is initially seen at 30° elevation. It rises vertically by 40 m without horizontal motion, after which the elevation is 45°. What was its initial altitude?
questions.explanation: Let horizontal distance be d and initial altitude h. Then h=d/√3 and h+40=d. Hence d(1−1/√3)=40, so d=20(3+√3) and h=d/√3=20(1+√3) m.

questions.stem: Evaluate log₁₀(1000).
Find log₂(32).
questions.explanation: Because2⁵=32, the logarithm is5.

questions.stem: For a>0 and a≠1, what is logₐ(1)?
questions.explanation: Since a⁰=1, logₐ(1)=0.

questions.stem: For a valid logarithm base b, evaluate log_b(b).
questions.explanation: Because b¹=b, log_b(b)=1.

questions.stem: Simplify log₁₀(10⁷).
questions.explanation: The logarithm and exponentiation with the same base cancel, giving7.

questions.stem: A scale value is 0.01 = 10⁻². What is its common logarithm?
questions.explanation: 0.01=10⁻², so the logarithm is−2.

questions.stem: If log₃x=4, what is x?
questions.explanation: The equation means x=3⁴=81.

questions.stem: Which identity is correct for positive x and y?
questions.explanation: The product law states logₐ(xy)=logₐx+logₐy.

questions.stem: Evaluate log₅(1/25).
If log₁₀2=0.3010, what is log₁₀20?
Solve log₂(x−1)=3.
Evaluate log₃81 + log₃(1/9).
questions.explanation: The terms are4 and−2, so the sum is2.

questions.stem: Simplify log₅125 − log₅5.
questions.explanation: Using the quotient law, this is log₅(125/5)=log₅25=2.

questions.stem: If logₓ64=3, with x>1, find x.
questions.explanation: x³=64, so x=4.

questions.stem: Evaluate log₄8.
questions.explanation: Write4=2² and8=2³. Therefore log₄8=3/2.

questions.stem: Express log₇11 using common logarithms.
questions.explanation: By the change-of-base formula, log₇11=log₁₀11/log₁₀7.

questions.stem: How many digits does 2²⁰ have, given log₁₀2≈0.30103?
questions.explanation: Digits=floor(log₁₀2²⁰)+1=floor(20×0.30103)+1=floor(6.0206)+1=7.

questions.stem: A solution has hydrogen-ion concentration 10⁻⁵ mol/L. Using pH=−log₁₀[H⁺], what is its pH?
questions.explanation: pH=−log₁₀(10⁻⁵)=5.

questions.stem: Solve log₁₀x + log₁₀(x−9)=1 for x>9.
questions.explanation: Combine logs: x(x−9)=10. Thus x²−9x−10=0=(x−10)(x+1). Domain x>9 leaves x=10.

questions.stem: If log₂3=a, express log₂24 in terms of a.
questions.explanation: 24=3×8, so log₂24=log₂3+log₂8=a+3.

questions.stem: Evaluate log₂5 × log₅8.
questions.explanation: Using logₐb×log_b c=logₐc, the product equals log₂8=3.

questions.stem: Find x if log₃x + log₃(x/3)=3, with x>0.
questions.explanation: Combine: log₃(x²/3)=3, so x²/3=27 and x²=81. Positivity gives x=9.

questions.stem: If log₁₀3=0.4771, approximate log₁₀27.
For what base b is log_b16=4?
questions.explanation: b⁴=16. A logarithm base is positive and not1, so b=2.

questions.stem:
What is the positive number x?

**Statement I:** log₂x is an integer between 4 and 6.

**Statement II:** x<40.
questions.explanation: Statement I forces log₂x=5, so x=32 and is sufficient. Statement II alone is not. Thus Statement I alone is sufficient.

options.label: Statement I alone is sufficient, but Statement II alone is not sufficient.
Statement II alone is sufficient, but Statement I alone is not sufficient.
Even both statements together are not sufficient.
Both statements together are sufficient, but neither statement alone is sufficient.

questions.stem: Evaluate log₂√32.
Solve (log₂x)² − 5log₂x + 6 = 0 for positive x. How many solutions are there?
questions.explanation: Let y=log₂x. Then(y−2)(y−3)=0, so y=2 or3, giving x=4 or8. There are2 solutions.

questions.stem: Solve logₓ16=4, where x>0 and x≠1.
questions.explanation: The equation means x⁴=16. Since a logarithm base must be positive, the only valid solution is x=2.

questions.stem: If log₂x + log₄x = 9, find x.
questions.explanation: Let y=log₂x. Since log₄x=y/2, we get3y/2=9, so y=6 and x=2⁶=64.

questions.stem: Find the greatest integer n such that log₂(n)<7.
questions.explanation: The inequality gives n<2⁷=128. The greatest integer is127.

questions.stem: Evaluate log₂3 · log₃4 · log₄8.
questions.explanation: The chain product telescopes to log₂8=3.

questions.stem: How many digits are there in 7⁵⁰, given log₁₀7≈0.845098?
For x>1, solve log₂(log₃x)=2.
questions.explanation: The outer equation gives log₃x=4. Hence x=3⁴=81.

questions.stem: If log₁₀2=a and log₁₀3=b, express log₁₀72.
Solve log₃(x+6) − log₃x = 1 for x>0.
questions.explanation: log₃((x+6)/x)=1 means(x+6)/x=3. Thus6=2x and x=3.

questions.stem: Evaluate log₂(3/2)+log₂(4/3)+log₂(5/4)+…+log₂(10/9).
questions.explanation: Combining logs gives log₂[(3/2)(4/3)…(10/9)]. The product telescopes to10/2=5, so the value is log₂5.

questions.stem:
What is x?

**Statement I:** log₂x + logₓ2 = 5/2.

**Statement II:** x>2.
questions.explanation: Let y=log₂x, so logₓ2=1/y. Statement I gives y+1/y=5/2, with y=2 or1/2, hence x=4 or√2. Statement II selects x=4. Both together are sufficient; neither alone is.

options.label: Even both statements together are not sufficient.
Both statements together are sufficient, but neither statement alone is sufficient.
Statement I alone is sufficient, but Statement II alone is not sufficient.
Statement II alone is sufficient, but Statement I alone is not sufficient.

questions.stem: How many binary information units are required for the 1,024-state system A?
After the eightfold expansion, what metric does System B attain?
questions.explanation: System B has8×1024=2³×2¹⁰=2¹³ states, so I=13.

questions.stem: Taking the square root of A’s state count changes System C’s metric to what value?
questions.explanation: System C has√1024=32=2⁵ states, so I=5.

questions.stem: By how much does the metric of B exceed that of C?
questions.explanation: The metrics are13 and5, so the difference is8.

questions.stem: If logₐb=2 and log_b c=3, what is logₐc?
questions.explanation: By chaining logarithms, logₐc=logₐb×log_b c=2×3=6.

questions.stem: Solve log₂x · log₄x · log₈x = 6 for x>1.
questions.explanation: Let y=log₂x. Then log₄x=y/2 and log₈x=y/3. Product=y³/6=6, so y³=36 and y=∛36. Therefore x=2^(∛36).

questions.stem: For x>0, x≠1, solve logₓ2 + log₂x = 2.
questions.explanation: Let y=log₂x, so logₓ2=1/y. Then y+1/y=2, giving(y−1)²=0. Thus y=1 and x=2.

questions.stem: Evaluate the product log₂3 · log₃4 · log₄5 · … · log₁₅16.
questions.explanation: The change-of-base ratios telescope: (ln3/ln2)(ln4/ln3)…(ln16/ln15)=ln16/ln2=log₂16=4.

questions.stem: How many real solutions does log₂(x²−5x+6)=0 have?
questions.explanation: The argument must equal1: x²−5x+6=1, so x²−5x+5=0. Its discriminant is25−20=5>0, giving two real roots. Both make the argument1 and are valid.

questions.stem: Express log₂45 in terms of a and b.
questions.explanation: 45=3²×5. Thus log₂45=2log₂3+log₂5=2a+(log₂3)(log₃5)=2a+ab=a(2+b).

questions.stem: Convert log₅8 to an expression involving a and b.
questions.explanation: Q=log₅8=log₃8/log₃5. Now log₃8=3log₃2=3/a, so Q=3/(ab).

questions.stem: Which expression equals log₂5?
questions.explanation: log₂5=log₂3×log₃5=ab.

questions.stem: Reduce log₆30 to an expression involving a and b.
questions.explanation: R=ln30/ln6. In base2, log₂30=1+a+ab and log₂6=1+a. Therefore R=(1+a+ab)/(1+a).

questions.stem: What remainder is obtained when 347 is divided by 9?
questions.explanation: 9×38 = 342, so the remainder is 347−342 = 5.

questions.stem: Which of the following integers is prime?
questions.explanation: 91=7×13, 93=3×31 and 95=5×19. The number 97 has no prime divisor not exceeding √97, so it is prime.

questions.stem: How many positive factors does 36 have?
questions.explanation: 36 = 2²×3². The number of positive factors is (2+1)(2+1)=9.

questions.stem: Which number is divisible by 11?
questions.explanation: For 2728, the alternating sum is (2+2)−(7+8)=−11, a multiple of 11. Hence 2728 is divisible by 11.

questions.stem: Find the sum of the first 20 positive integers.
What is the smallest positive multiple of 7 greater than 100?
questions.explanation: 7×14=98 and 7×15=105. Therefore the smallest such multiple is 105.

questions.stem: The product of two odd integers is always odd. What is the parity of the sum of that product and an odd integer?
questions.explanation: Odd×odd is odd, and odd+odd is even.

questions.stem: What is the units digit of 7³?
questions.explanation: 7³ = 343, whose units digit is 3.

questions.stem: How many integers lie strictly between −4 and 5?
questions.explanation: The integers are −3,−2,−1,0,1,2,3,4: eight integers.

questions.stem: If a two-digit number has tens digit 6 and units digit 4, what is the number?
questions.explanation: A two-digit number with digits a and b equals 10a+b. Thus 10×6+4 = 64.

questions.stem: What least digit should replace * in 53*4 so that the number is divisible by 9?
questions.explanation: The digit sum is 5+3+*+4 = 12+*. It must be a multiple of 9. The least digit making this 18 is 6.

questions.stem: How many trailing zeros are there in 75!?
questions.explanation: Trailing zeros equal the number of factors 5: floor(75/5)+floor(75/25)=15+3=18.

questions.stem: Find the units digit of 3²⁷.
questions.explanation: Units digits of powers of 3 cycle as 3,9,7,1 with period 4. Since 27 leaves remainder 3 modulo 4, the units digit is the third in the cycle, 7.

questions.stem: How many multiples of 6 are there from 100 through 500, inclusive?
questions.explanation: The count is floor(500/6)−floor(99/6)=83−16=67.

questions.stem: What is the remainder when 2¹⁰ is divided by 7?
questions.explanation: 2³=8≡1 (mod 7). Thus 2⁹≡1 and 2¹⁰≡2, so the remainder is 2.

questions.stem: How many positive divisors does 720 have?
questions.explanation: 720 = 2⁴×3²×5. Hence the divisor count is (4+1)(2+1)(1+1)=30.

questions.stem: Find the sum of all positive divisors of 18.
Which of the following can be the last two digits of a perfect square?
questions.explanation: 73² = 5329, so 29 can occur. A square cannot end in 2, 3, 7 or 8, ruling out the other endings.

questions.stem: The sum of five consecutive integers is 215. What is the largest integer?
questions.explanation: The middle integer is the average, 215/5=43. The five integers are 41 through 45, so the largest is 45.

questions.stem: A positive integer leaves remainder 4 when divided by 7. What remainder does three times the integer leave when divided by 7?
questions.explanation: If n≡4 (mod 7), then 3n≡12≡5 (mod 7).

questions.stem: How many three-digit positive integers are divisible by 13?
questions.explanation: The largest is 13×76=988 and the smallest is 13×8=104. Count = 76−8+1 = 69.

questions.stem: Find the greatest integer n for which 2ⁿ divides 96.
questions.explanation: 96 = 2⁵×3. Therefore the greatest exponent is n=5.

questions.stem: A number written in base 5 as 243₅ has what value in base 10?
What is the digital root of 987654?
questions.explanation: The digit sum is 9+8+7+6+5+4=39, and 3+9=12, then 1+2=3. The digital root is 3.

questions.stem:
Is the positive integer n divisible by 12?

**Statement I:** n is divisible by 3 and by 4.

**Statement II:** n is divisible by 6 and is even.
questions.explanation: Statement I is sufficient because 3 and 4 are coprime, so divisibility by both implies divisibility by 12. Statement II only implies divisibility by 6; n=6 is a counterexample. Thus Statement I alone is sufficient.

options.label: Statement II alone is sufficient, but Statement I alone is not sufficient.
Statement I alone is sufficient, but Statement II alone is not sufficient.
Even both statements together are not sufficient.
Both statements together are sufficient, but neither statement alone is sufficient.

questions.stem: What is the remainder when 99999 is divided by 37?
questions.explanation: 999 = 37×27, so 99900 is divisible by 37. The remainder of 99999 is therefore the remainder of 99, which is 99−74=25.

questions.stem: Find the least positive integer that leaves remainders 2, 3 and 4 when divided by 3, 4 and 5, respectively.
questions.explanation: The conditions say n+1 is divisible by 3,4 and 5. Their LCM is 60, so the least positive n is 59.

questions.stem: What is the remainder when 7¹⁰⁰ is divided by 13?
questions.explanation: By Fermat, 7¹²≡1 (mod 13). Since 100≡4 (mod 12), 7¹⁰⁰≡7⁴. Now 7²=49≡10 and 7⁴≡100≡9, so the remainder is 9.

questions.stem: How many positive divisors of 360 are multiples of 12?
questions.explanation: 360=2³×3²×5. A divisor multiple of 12=2²×3 must use exponent of 2 equal to 2 or 3 (2 choices), exponent of 3 equal to 1 or 2 (2 choices), and exponent of 5 equal to 0 or 1 (2 choices). Count = 8.

questions.stem: What is the highest power of 3 that divides 100!?
questions.explanation: The exponent of 3 in 100! is floor(100/3)+floor(100/9)+floor(100/27)+floor(100/81)=33+11+3+1=48.

questions.stem: A positive integer has exactly 15 positive divisors and is of the form pᵃqᵇ for distinct primes p and q with a≥b≥1. What are a and b?
questions.explanation: The divisor count is (a+1)(b+1)=15=5×3. Hence a+1=5 and b+1=3, giving a=4 and b=2.

questions.stem: How many integers from 1 to 1000 are divisible by 4 or 6 but not by both?
questions.explanation: Multiples of 4:250; of 6:166; of both (LCM 12):83. Exactly one set has 250+166−2×83 = 250 integers.

questions.stem: Find the least positive integer n such that n is a perfect square and 72n is a perfect cube.
questions.explanation: 72=2³×3². Let n have even exponents and make total exponents multiples of 3. For 2, add exponent 0; for 3, add exponent 4, since 2+4=6. Thus n=3⁴=81.

questions.stem: The number 4a7b is divisible by both 9 and 11, where a and b are digits. What is a+b?
questions.explanation: Divisibility by 11 gives (4+7)−(a+b) = 0 or ±11. Since a+b is between 0 and 18, a+b=11. This also makes the total digit sum 4+7+11=22, not divisible by 9, so use difference ±11: 11−(a+b)=−11 gives a+b=22 impossible. Therefore no such digit pair exists.

questions.stem: What is the remainder when 1! + 2! + 3! + … + 20! is divided by 10?
questions.explanation: For k≥5, k! ends in zero and contributes remainder 0 modulo 10. The sum 1!+2!+3!+4! = 1+2+6+24 = 33 leaves remainder 3.

questions.stem: A three-digit number is divisible by 7. Reversing its digits gives a number 198 greater than the original. Which of the following can be the original number?
questions.explanation: For a number 100a+10b+c, reversal difference is 99(c−a)=198, so c−a=2. Among the options, 357 reverses to 753, a difference of 396; 476 reverses to 674, a difference of 198, and 476=7×68. Thus 476 works.

questions.stem:
What is the remainder when the positive integer n is divided by 12?

**Statement I:** n leaves remainder 1 when divided by 3.

**Statement II:** n leaves remainder 5 when divided by 8.
questions.explanation: Statement I allows residues 1,4,7,10 modulo 12. Statement II gives residues congruent to 5 modulo 8, which can be 5 or 1 modulo 12 depending on the integer. Together, solve n≡1 (mod3) and n≡5 (mod8): the unique residue modulo 24 is 13, so modulo 12 the remainder is 1. Both together are sufficient.

options.label: Even both statements together are not sufficient.
Statement I alone is sufficient, but Statement II alone is not sufficient.
Statement II alone is sufficient, but Statement I alone is not sufficient.
Both statements together are sufficient, but neither statement alone is sufficient.

questions.stem: What is the token N?
questions.explanation: Numbers congruent to 3 modulo 5 in the interval can be checked modulo 7. The unique odd solution is 123: 123 mod 5 = 3 and 123 mod 7 = 4.

questions.stem: What remainder does N² leave when divided by 7?
questions.explanation: N≡4 (mod7), so N²≡16≡2 (mod7).

questions.stem: How many positive divisors does N have?
questions.explanation: N=123=3×41, a product of two distinct primes. Its divisor count is (1+1)(1+1)=4.

questions.stem: What is the digital root of 4N?
questions.explanation: 4N=492. Its digit sum is 4+9+2=15 and then 1+5=6, so the digital root is 6.

questions.stem: What remainder does the sum 1 + 2 + 3 + … + 100 leave when divided by 13?
questions.explanation: The sum is 100×101/2 = 5050. Since 13×388 = 5044, the remainder is 6.

questions.stem: What is the remainder when 2^(2^10) is divided by 17?
questions.explanation: Since 2⁸=256≡1 (mod17), reduce the exponent modulo 8. Because 2¹⁰ is divisible by 8, 2^(2^10)≡2⁰≡1 (mod17).

questions.stem: How many positive divisors of 2⁸×3⁶×5⁴ are perfect squares but not perfect fourth powers?
questions.explanation: For a square divisor, exponents may be 0,2,…: 5 choices for 2, 4 for 3 and 3 for 5, giving 60. For a fourth power, exponents are multiples of 4: 3×2×2=12. Excluding fourth powers leaves 60−12=48.

questions.stem: Find the smallest positive integer n for which 2n is a perfect square and 3n is a perfect cube.
questions.explanation: For the exponent of 2 in n, 2n being a square requires it to be odd, while 3n being a cube requires it to be a multiple of 3; the least is 3. For the exponent of 3, the square condition requires an even exponent and the cube condition requires e+1 to be a multiple of 3; the least is 2. Hence n=2³×3²=72.

questions.stem: How many ordered pairs of positive integers (a,b) satisfy 1/a + 1/b = 1/6?
questions.explanation: Rearrange: ab−6a−6b=0, so (a−6)(b−6)=36. Each positive divisor d of 36 gives a−6=d and b−6=36/d. Since 36 has 9 positive divisors, there are 9 ordered pairs.

questions.stem: A three-digit base-b numeral 121_b equals 16 in base 10. What is b?
questions.explanation: 121_b = b²+2b+1 = (b+1)². Setting this equal to 16 gives b+1=4, so b=3. The digits 1 and 2 are valid in base 3.

questions.stem: How many eligible divisors d are there?
questions.explanation: Divisibility by 60=2²×3×5 requires exponents at least 2,1,1. Choices are 5 for the exponent of 2 (2 through 6), 4 for 3 (1 through 4), and 2 for 5 (1 through 2): 5×4×2=40.

questions.stem: Among the eligible divisors, how many are perfect squares?
questions.explanation: Square exponents must be even. For 2: 2,4,6 (3 choices); for 3: 2,4 (2 choices); for 5: only 2 (1 choice). Count = 3×2×1 = 6.

questions.stem: Among the eligible divisors, how many have exactly 36 positive divisors?
questions.explanation: For d=2ᵃ3ᵇ5ᶜ with a∈{2,…,6}, b∈{1,…,4}, c∈{1,2}, require (a+1)(b+1)(c+1)=36. If c=1, need (a+1)(b+1)=18, giving (6,3) so (a,b)=(5,2). If c=2, need product 12, giving (4,3) or (3,4), so (a,b)=(3,2) or (2,3). Thus there are 3.

questions.stem: Complete the arithmetic progression 2, 5, 8, 11, __.
questions.explanation: Each term increases by3, so the next term is14.

questions.stem: Which value follows 1, 4, 9, 16, 25 in the sequence?
questions.explanation: These are consecutive squares1² through5². The next is6²=36.

questions.stem: Identify the odd one out: 16, 25, 36, 45.
questions.explanation: 16,25 and36 are perfect squares;45 is not.

questions.stem: A counter displays 3, 6, 12, 24, … by applying the same rule. What is its next display?
questions.explanation: Every term is twice the previous term, so24×2=48.

questions.stem: Fill the blank in 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, __.
questions.explanation: Each term is the sum of the previous two. Thus5+8=13.

questions.stem: The list 50, 45, 40, 35 continues regularly. What comes next?
questions.explanation: The sequence decreases by5 each time, giving30.

questions.stem: Determine the next triangular number after 1, 3, 6, 10, 15.
questions.explanation: Successive additions are2,3,4,5; add6 next to get21.

questions.stem: What is the missing term in the odd-number sequence 7, 9, 11, __, 15?
questions.explanation: Consecutive odd numbers differ by2, so the missing term is13.

questions.stem: Continue 81, 27, 9, 3, … using its constant ratio.
questions.explanation: Each term is divided by3. Therefore the next term is1.

questions.stem: Which term does not belong in 8, 27, 64, 100, 125?
questions.explanation: 8=2³,27=3³,64=4³ and125=5³. The number100 is not a cube.

questions.stem: Find the missing value in 4, 9, 16, 25, __, 49.
questions.explanation: The terms are squares2²,3²,4²,5²,6²,7². The missing value is36.

questions.stem: A sequence begins 2, 6, 12, 20, 30. Which number should appear next?
questions.explanation: The terms are n(n+1) for n=1,2,3,4,5. The next is6×7=42.

questions.stem: Resolve the blank in 5, 10, 8, 16, 14, 28, __.
questions.explanation: The operations alternate ×2,−2. After28, subtract2 to obtain26.

questions.stem: What succeeds 3, 7, 15, 31, 63?
questions.explanation: Each term is twice the preceding term plus1. Thus2×63+1=127.

questions.stem: Complete 11, 13, 17, 19, 23, __ with the next appropriate term.
questions.explanation: These are consecutive prime numbers beginning at11. The next prime is29.

questions.stem: Select the term that breaks the pattern 2, 6, 12, 20, 31, 42.
questions.explanation: The intended pattern n(n+1) gives2,6,12,20,30,42. Hence31 is the incorrect term.
