passages.body: A survey boat has a still-water speed of 18 km/h. It travels 48 km downstream in a 6 km/h current, waits 30 minutes, then returns upstream. Halfway through the return, measured by distance, the current weakens from 6 km/h to 3 km/h.
passages.title: Survey-boat field trip

passages.body: A non-leap project year begins on Monday, 1 January. Reviews are scheduled on the first Monday of every month and on the final day of each quarter.
passages.title: Project-year schedule

passages.body: A leap year begins on Friday. A system runs a full backup on every Monday and a quarterly archive on the last day of March, June, September and December.
passages.title: Leap-year operations

passages.body: A data-labeling project requires 7,20,000 labels. Team X has 40 labelers at 50 labels/hour for 6 hours/day. Team Y has 30 labelers at 60 labels/hour for 5 hours/day. Both work together for 10 days. After that, X loses 10 labelers while Y’s hourly productivity rises by 20%; daily hours remain unchanged.
passages.title: Data-labeling capacity caselet

passages.body: A robotics startup invests ₹10,00,000 at the start of Year 1. The fund gains 12% in Year 1, loses 5% in Year 2, and gains 10% in Year 3. At the end of Year 1, immediately after the gain is credited, ₹2,00,000 is withdrawn. No other cash flow occurs. All annual changes apply to the balance present during that year.
passages.title: Robotics startup reserve

passages.body: A telemetry unit stores three readings: A = 0.625 MB, B = 1.375 MB and C = 0.0875 MB. Compression reduces A by 0.125 of its original size, reduces B to 0.8 of its original size, and leaves C unchanged.
passages.title: Telemetry compression

passages.body: A data logger records a value x. Its display rounds x to 2.73 at two decimal places. A derived value y = 1/x is then shown to four decimal places. Assume ordinary round-to-nearest conventions.
passages.title: Rounding bounds and reciprocals

passages.body: A factory schedules maintenance for machines A, B and C every 18, 30 and 45 days, respectively. All three are serviced together on 1 January. Ignore calendar-month lengths and count days continuously.
passages.title: Maintenance cycles

passages.body: Three positive integers are A=2⁴×3²×5, B=2³×3⁴×7 and C=2⁵×3×5²×7. Let H be their HCF and L their LCM.
passages.title: Prime-exponent model

passages.body: A data-compression metric is defined by I=log₂(N), where N is the number of equally likely states. System A has 1024 states. System B has 8 times as many states as System A. System C has the square root of System A’s number of states.
passages.title: Information-scale caselet

passages.body: Let a=log₂3 and b=log₃5. Define P=log₂45, Q=log₅8, and R=log₆30. Expressions may be left in terms of a and b.
passages.title: Chained logarithms

passages.body: A security token is a positive integer N satisfying N ≡ 3 (mod 5), N ≡ 4 (mod 7), and 100 < N < 150. The token is also required to be odd.
passages.title: Modular security token

passages.body: Let M = 2⁶×3⁴×5². A divisor d of M is selected subject to the condition that d is divisible by 60.
passages.title: Constrained divisors

passages.body: A sequence is defined by a₁=3 and aₙ₊₁=2aₙ+n for n≥1.
passages.title: Recurrence caselet

passages.body: Define b₁=2, b₂=5, and bₙ=bₙ₋₁+2bₙ₋₂ for n≥3. Define cₙ=bₙ/bₙ₋₁ whenever the ratio is formed.
passages.title: Second-order recurrence

passages.body: Three engineering graduates start a fabrication unit on 1 April. A invests ₹1,20,000 for the full 12 months. B invests ₹90,000 initially and adds ₹30,000 after 4 months. C joins after 3 months with ₹1,60,000 but withdraws ₹40,000 after another 5 months. The year’s divisible profit, after all salaries and charges, is ₹4,84,000.
passages.title: Fabrication-unit partnership caselet

passages.body: A semiconductor plant starts a week with 1,00,000 wafers in process. Stage A rejects 4% of the wafers entering it. Stage B rejects 5% of the wafers that survive Stage A. Of the wafers surviving Stage B, 10% are classified as premium grade. The plant sells every premium wafer for ₹1,200 and every other finished wafer for ₹800. In a proposed improvement, Stage A rejection is reduced by 25% of its current rejection rate, while Stage B rejection is reduced by 20% of its current rejection rate. The input volume and selling prices remain unchanged.
passages.title: Semiconductor yield improvement caselet

passages.body: A 9,000-litre process tank has inlet A delivering 300 L/min, inlet B delivering 200 L/min, and a drain removing 100 L/min. A and B start together. After 10 minutes B is closed. Five minutes later the drain is also closed, while A continues.
passages.title: Process-tank valve schedule

passages.body: A project team has five members A, B, C, D, and E. Their current ages are in arithmetic progression. The youngest is 22, the oldest is 38. Two years from now a 30-year-old member F will join, while the then-oldest member will leave.
passages.title: Project-team age caselet

passages.body: A three-digit access code has digits a, b and c from left to right. The digit sum is 15. The first digit is two more than the last digit, and the number formed by the first two digits is 11 greater than the number formed by the last two digits.
passages.title: Three-digit access code

passages.body: Two positive integers A and B satisfy A>B. Their sum is 70. The sum of their squares is 2500. A third integer C is the geometric mean of A and B whenever that mean is integral.
passages.title: Linked integer constraints

passages.body: Train P is 240 m long and travels at 72 km/h. Train Q is 160 m long and travels at 54 km/h. They first move in opposite directions, then later in the same direction. A platform used in the test is 360 m long.
passages.title: Railway timing test caselet

passages.body: A campus store buys 500 scientific calculators at ₹800 each. It marks each calculator 40% above cost. During the first sale, 60% of the stock is sold at a 15% discount on marked price. Of the remaining calculators, 20 are damaged and cannot be sold. The rest are sold at a 25% discount on marked price. Ignore taxes and any other costs.
passages.title: Campus calculator inventory caselet

passages.body: Four runners use a 400 m track. A runs at 8 m/s, B at 6 m/s, C at 5 m/s, and D at 4 m/s. A and B start together from the line in the same direction. C starts from the line in the opposite direction. D starts 100 m ahead of the line in A’s direction.
passages.title: Track-session caselet

passages.body: A robotics lab allocates 360 compute-hours among Vision, Control and Simulation. Vision:Control = 3:2. Control:Simulation = 4:5. During execution, Vision uses 10% fewer hours than allocated, Control uses exactly its allocation, and Simulation uses 20% more than allocated. Any unused Vision hours may be reassigned to Simulation after the initial run.
passages.title: Robotics compute-hour allocation

passages.body: An engineering incubator has ₹12,00,000 available on 1 April. It places 40% in Deposit A at 8% simple interest for 18 months, 35% in Deposit B at 10% simple interest for 1 year, and the balance in Deposit C at 12% simple interest for 9 months. Interest is calculated only on the original amount in each deposit.
passages.title: Incubator treasury allocation

passages.body: A coding challenge assigns the score S = 4C − W + B, where C is the number of correct answers, W the number of wrong answers and B a bonus. A participant has C = 18 and W = 7. The bonus is defined by B = (3⁴ − 5²)/(2³ − 1).
passages.title: Scoring expression

passages.body: Define a sequence by a₁ = 2 and aₙ₊₁ = 1 + 1/aₙ. All values are exact rational numbers.
passages.title: Nested reciprocal sequence

passages.body: A square-based storage module has square floor area 2025 m². A cube-shaped container has volume 3375 m³. Both dimensions are exact.
passages.title: Root-based dimensions

passages.body: Let A be the least positive integer such that 540A is a perfect square. Let B be the least positive integer such that 540B is a perfect cube.
passages.title: Minimal root completion

passages.body: A graduate invests in two listed companies. She buys 400 Alpha shares at ₹75 with 1% brokerage; Alpha has face value ₹10 and pays 20% dividend. She buys 300 Beta shares at ₹120 with 2% brokerage; Beta has face value ₹100 and pays 12% dividend. At year-end Alpha trades at ₹84 and Beta at ₹114. Ignore selling brokerage unless a question explicitly asks for it.
passages.title: Two-stock portfolio caselet

passages.body: Let p=√3+√2 and q=√3−√2. Note that p and q are positive conjugate surds.
passages.title: Conjugate-surds caselet

passages.body: Define u=2+√3. Since (2+√3)(2−√3)=1, its reciprocal is u⁻¹=2−√3. For n≥0, let Sₙ=uⁿ+u⁻ⁿ.
passages.title: Surd-power recurrence

passages.body: A campus shuttle follows a 210 km intercity route. It covers the first 60 km at 40 km/h, stops 15 minutes, covers the next 90 km at 60 km/h, and covers the final 60 km at 80 km/h. On the return trip it uses a constant running speed of 70 km/h and stops once for 30 minutes.
passages.title: Campus shuttle round-trip caselet

passages.body: A software migration has 1,200 task-points. Team Alpha has 8 engineers, each delivering 6 task-points per day. Team Beta has 6 engineers, each delivering 5 task-points per day. Both teams start together. After 10 days, two Alpha engineers are reassigned. After another 5 days, automation increases the productivity of every remaining engineer in both teams by 20%. Assume constant productivity within each phase and no rework.
passages.title: Software migration work-rate caselet

passages.body: A university must make three future payments: ₹54,000 after 1 year, ₹92,000 after 2 years, and ₹1,30,000 after 3 years. For budgeting, it values every payment at 8% simple interest, discounting each independently to today.
passages.title: University capital-budgeting caselet
